dossier.public_summary: The dip changes depth between visits and alternates odd versus even between ~2392 ppm and ~1235 ppm, which points to an eclipsing binary at twice the period. One transit is missing entirely, and there is no centroid measurement to show the signal is on the target. Together this is best explained by a blend or false alarm, not a planet of 3.1 Earth radii.

reasons.why: Depth is inconsistent across the four transits and the signal is carried almost entirely by the top three, with epoch 2 requiring no transit. Not consistent with a repeating planet.

No difference imaging to place the dip on the target, so a neighbour blend cannot be ruled out. neighbours plausible_within_1px=1 supports a blended-false-positive scenario, consistent with xgboost planet_rank=0.07.
